label: rewrite keeps the old facts?
instructions: Is every part of the old memory in quoted_old that is still true after the messages in quoted_source kept in the new memory in quoted_new? A detail the messages changed counts as kept when the new memory gives its new value.
true: Yes: everything the old memory said that is still true is in the new one, though it may be worded differently, extended, or updated where the messages changed it.
false: No: the new memory drops or blurs something from the old one that the messages didn't change.

true: "Kai quit coffee." → "Kai quit coffee last month; temple headaches when he cut back."
"Kai's exam is on Monday." → "Kai's exam moved to Wednesday." (the messages moved it)
false: "Kai's sister Mia is a nurse in Ipoh." → "Kai's sister is a nurse."

state_note: memory D15: one request per rewrite; p >= t_keep supersedes, else the new line is inserted beside the old one. v2 (phase 10, the user's choice): a changed detail counts as kept. v3: t_keep 0.35 by D40's rule on the set with changed values (test: lossy through 0.04, changed values 7/7 supersede; m13.md).
